# Import Figma files

* * *

[Copy link to heading](https://www.canva.com/help/importing-figma-files/#exporting-your-figma-files)

## Exporting your Figma files

- **Figma Design files:** we recommend uploading your individual assets into Canva as separate PNGs/ SVGs. Follow the steps found in [Uploading media from your device](https://www.canva.com/help/upload-media/).
- **FigJam files:** you can import them into Canva via PDF upload.

You can also export individual frames from Figma files and then upload these into Canva as media items.

[Copy link to heading](https://www.canva.com/help/importing-figma-files/#importing-your-figjam-files-via-pdf)

## Importing your FigJam files via PDF

Easily import your FigJam files to Canva by **any of the following** methods:

[Copy link to heading](https://www.canva.com/help/importing-figma-files/#from-the-homepage-)

### From the homepage

###### Quick tip

You can upload files directly from the homepage.

[Take me there](https://canva.me/pp-pdf-editor)

1. Drag and drop your PDF to the [homepage](https://www.canva.com/).
2. On the top corner of the homepage banner, click the **Upload** button. Drag your file to the Upload section or click on **browse**.
3. On the side menu of the homepage, click

**Projects**. Drag your file to the page to upload it, or click on the **Add new** button.

Once done, click on the imported PDF to open it in the Canva editor.

[Copy link to heading](https://www.canva.com/help/importing-figma-files/#from-the-editor)

### From the editor

1. Drag and drop your PDF to the editor.
2. On the top corner of the editor, click on **File** \>

**Upload a file**.
3. On the editor side panel, click on the

**Uploads** tab, then click on **Upload files**. Select the files you want to upload, or drag and drop them in the **Uploads** tab.

To use the file in your design, click on it from the

**Projects** tab in the editor side panel.

To find all your uploads, select

**Projects** from the homepage side panel. On the

**owner dropdown, select your name to view your projects or**

**Any owner to view all projects, then click on the**

**Uploads folder, where you can also download or delete them.**

[Copy link to heading](https://www.canva.com/help/importing-figma-files/#from-the-pdf-editor-and-converter-pages)

### From the PDF editor and converter pages

There are several pages dedicated to uploading your PDF (i.e. [PDF editor](https://www.canva.com/pdf-editor/), [PDF converter](https://www.canva.com/features/pdf-converter/)). From one of these pages, follow these steps:

1. Click on

**Upload your file** or

**Upload your PDF**.
2. Choose the file from your device.
3. Log in to your Canva account to continue.

The uploaded PDF will open in the editor where you can revise and [download it as another file type.](https://www.canva.com/help/download-or-purchase/)

You can import files of up to 100MB in size.

For more information on what to expect when uploading PDFs, see [Importing PDFs](https://www.canva.com/help/pdf-import/).

# An Dead Easy Export From Canva To Figma

[![Pingu Noot](https://miro.medium.com/v2/da:true/resize:fill:32:32/0*xUJyC6gFvsQz0qYw)](https://medium.com/@pingubustanut?source=post_page---byline--8765490cb922---------------------------------------)

[Pingu Noot](https://medium.com/@pingubustanut?source=post_page---byline--8765490cb922---------------------------------------)

Follow

4 min read

·

Sep 5, 2022

36

4

[Listen](https://medium.com/m/signin?actionUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fmedium.com%2Fplans%3Fdimension%3Dpost_audio_button%26postId%3D8765490cb922&operation=register&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmedium.com%2Fdesign-bootcamp%2Fan-dead-easy-export-from-canva-to-figma-8765490cb922&source=---header_actions--8765490cb922---------------------post_audio_button------------------)

Share

Canva is one of the greatest design tools of all time. I use it daily for creating marketing infographics and sprucing up social posts.

I also use Figma. In two ways. The first is as a central repository. The second is as a more powerful design tool that does a lot Canva can’t. Figma is home base. It’s where I keep things together and how I grab an easy link to share and show what I’ve done.

Sometimes, when I really feeling like over-delivering, I’ll even create a prototype with all the pages I exported from Canva. Now that’s a nice link to share with a client!

**The problem is…**

The workflow for moving designs between Canva and Figma is terrible.

Until recently, you could only export top-level pages.

These are top level pages

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:586/1*tEGNMVUKCPwmModWUlNA6Q.gif)

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:87/1*DPOhFanwjMSB5Q9ul6EmPg.png)

This is what Canva exports.

If you want an illustration, by itself, you need to create a new page that’s the same size as that illustration. This scales like a patron of the Heart Attack Grill. Does that mean it scales well? or poorly?🤔

Then they added the option to export selection. You can select several text elements, right click, and you’ll find it.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*Ba1P_SukKh__gZt7TBQgpQ.png)

It’s better than exporting page level elements, but all the text comes out as PNGs which is a little useless.

You can’t copy and paste because this:

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*OrYQmaYu06ps8wqaY4rKeA.png)

Becomes this:

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*CuZwwvURQfmFSVmmPxl_PA.png)

### What I really what are all my Canva designs in Figma

I want to use Canva’s amazing illustrations everywhere, and I want to be able to edit them once there in Figma too.

The forums told me, I was not alone.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*xME4bn7oh9fZsxqT-qnjEQ.png)

right!!!

Unfortunately, I found no help.

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:430/1*9vAaDXCgbQv9wZcK0we8kw.png)

Sheep

After intense an googling montages. I have found a legitimate solution. A real life way to export between Canva and Figma.

Actually, I found the only way.

### TL;DR: there’s a tool called Magicul that lets you convert Canva files to Figma.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*cH0N0FMZQsSuSTLgWw3srw.png)

This hasn’t just saved me so much time. It’s given me the ability to do something that was impossible to do before.

## Get Pingu Noot’s stories in your inbox

Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer.

Subscribe

Subscribe

Remember me for faster sign in

[https://magicul.io/converter/canva-to-figma](https://magicul.io/converter/canva-to-figma)

It’s in beta and conversions are free. So I thought, why not give it a shot?

### Wanna see?

I’ll convert this from Canva to Figma.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*7BIkVhRc7wsM16e5MHDYuQ.png)

A free template.

**1 — Export all pages from Canva into PDF format**

Download ➡ File Type ➡ PDF Standard ➡ Download

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:381/1*fRaI3iKM0N5EN3F9I8O60w.gif)

Sign up the beta. I was approved within the hour.

Go here:

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*NoUC8wmNnfGZ5InKUBFjAQ.png)

After the conversion, open the file in Figma.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*w8j2CJJnh-Ca1K9Pgs-Lvw.png)

And OMG what are these!

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:252/1*PimSTpuOKYHLbse8CQlyyg.png)

A layer structure from Canva. Is the search over?

It’s verbose. Every letter is its own shape.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*pWgTUP-r54F2kTosqflWoA.png)

But that’s kinda cool. Lets you do cool stuff with it, like this:

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*AWD0tZ8SkkR1PHPKuIiMdw.png)

Unleashing the power of Figma it’s possible to take the design in a completely different direction.

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:635/1*Q0g5tEy_svi3_IvFH2jgjQ.png)

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*SPE9rs2VvRYrBalAJGnz5A.png)

Cool, right!

I suspect this is a fantastic way to add prototyping to my Canva designs as well.

Now I’m considering writing an article about that.

**Let’s Wrap It Up**

Thanks for making it to the end. I hope you enjoyed and learned something new.

Do you know another way to work between Canva and Figma? I want to try it.

# [How to Convert Canva Designs to Figma (2026 Full Guide)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JCWCZyIOYG8)

**Visibility**: Public
**Uploaded by**: [Tutorialytics](http://www.youtube.com/@Tutorialytics)

## Description

```
In today's video, we cover, How to Convert Canva Designs to Figma.


Convert Canva to Figma, Canva to Figma tutorial, How to export from Canva for Figma, Canva design to Figma, Transfer Canva to Figma, Import Canva to Figma, Canva Figma workflow, Canva to Figma migration, Canva design transfer, Figma from Canva, Use Canva designs in Figma, Canva to Figma integration, Canva Figma comparison, Canva alternatives for Figma, Design tools comparison, Graphic design workflow, UI design, UX design, Web design, Digital design, Design software, Canva tips and tricks, Figma tutorials, Design software tutorial, Canva export settings, Figma import guide, Canva to Figma best practices, Canva limitations, Figma features, Free design tools
```

## Transcript

In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to convert Canva designs to Figma. We'll take a design you made in Canva, turn it into an SVG, and bring it into Figma so you can edit it there. This approach works best for logos, icons, and simple graphics. Just keep in mind that since we're starting from a PNG, the conversion to SVG will trace shapes, and outline text, so it won't preserve live text or perfectly maintain every effect. With that in mind, let's get started. First, open your design in Canva. At the top right, click share, then choose download. This opens the export panel for your current design. If your design has multiple pages, pick just the pages you want to move over. It helps to tidy up your Canva layout first, turning off any elements you don't plan to transfer. If your design has a background color you don't want, you can remove it later, but it's easier to handle it now. Next, select PNG as the file type and download it. PNG is a good source format for tracing because it supports transparency and high resolution. If you see a size or scale option, choose a larger export like 2x to give the converter more detail to work with. If your design needs a transparent background in Figma, enable the transparent background option before exporting. Then download the file to a location you can find easily. Now, open a PNG to SVG converter in your browser and upload the PNG you just saved. Use a reputable converter and check any file size limits. If your design spans multiple pages, export and convert each page separately so you can keep things organized. Clean, high contrast artwork tends to convert more accurately, so higher resolution PNGs usually produce better SVG results. Click convert, then download the resulting SVG. Many converters offer settings like color count, smoothing, or path precision. If the preview looks too jagged or too simplified, try adjusting those settings and converting again. Make sure you're downloading the file in SVG format and give it a clear file name so you can recognize it later in Figma. Finally, open your Figma file and drag and drop the SVG onto the canvas. The artwork should arrive as editable vector paths. You can ungroup elements, adjust fills and strokes, and tweak colors as needed. Any text from Canva will be outlined, so plan to replace it with native Figma text if you need to edit wording. Take a moment to check scale, align elements, and rename layers to keep your file tidy. That's it. Export from Canva as PNG, convert to SVG, and drop it into Figma for editing. Save your Figma file and you're ready to continue designing.
